note: The simulator actions a trainee may start by speaking (DT-251, ADR-0027). Each entry is an action that already exists on the tablet; `means` is the plain description the language model reads to decide whether a sentence is that action. Only conversational actions are here. Physical or safety-critical actions (confirming identity, reporting a mismatch, reading the wristband, opening the notes, attaching or removing a sensor, measuring) are never started by speech: they stay gestures or tablet buttons, so a spoken sentence cannot earn credit for a physical act. The engine, not the model, decides whether the action is allowed now and what it changes.

actions.label: Introduce yourself
actions.means: The trainee greets the patient and says who they are and what they are going to do.

actions.label: Ask name and date of birth
actions.means: The trainee asks the patient to say their full name and their date of birth.

actions.label: Ask about allergies
actions.means: The trainee asks whether the patient has any allergies.

actions.label: Ask what happened
actions.means: The trainee asks what happened when the patient had an allergic reaction, or what the reaction was like.

actions.label: Ask why she is here
actions.means: The trainee asks why the patient has come in, or what the operation is for.

actions.label: Ask about home support
actions.means: The trainee asks who will take the patient home or look after them at home after the operation.

actions.label: Main problem (pain)
actions.means: The trainee asks about the main problem or pain: where it is, when it started, what it is like.

actions.label: Red flags
actions.means: The trainee asks about warning symptoms such as fever, yellow eyes, dark urine, pale stools, vomiting or itching.

actions.label: Other illnesses
actions.means: The trainee asks about other illnesses or medical conditions the patient has, for example diabetes, heart or blood pressure problems.

actions.label: Medicines
actions.means: The trainee asks which tablets, medicines or blood thinners the patient takes.

actions.label: Herbal remedies
actions.means: The trainee asks about herbal remedies or supplements.

actions.label: Previous anaesthetic
actions.means: The trainee asks whether the patient has had an operation or an anaesthetic before and whether it went well.

actions.label: Family anaesthetic
actions.means: The trainee asks whether anyone in the family has had problems with an anaesthetic.

actions.label: Smoking
actions.means: The trainee asks whether the patient smokes.

actions.label: Alcohol
actions.means: The trainee asks about alcohol.

actions.label: Last food
actions.means: The trainee asks when the patient last ate.

actions.label: Last drink
actions.means: The trainee asks when the patient last had something to drink.

actions.label: Pregnancy (privately)
actions.means: The trainee asks, privately, about pregnancy or the last period.

actions.label: Summarise
actions.means: The trainee sums up what the patient has told them and checks it is right.

actions.label: Ask pain score
actions.means: The trainee asks the patient to give their pain a number out of ten.

actions.label: Ask nurse for a wristband
actions.means: The trainee asks the nurse to bring or put on an identity wristband for the patient.
